facts.text: Buses to and from Tashkurgan stop in Sost, with driving time taking roughly 5 hours.
facts.quote: Buses to and from Tashkurgan stop in Sost

facts.text: The usual jumping off point for the Karakoram Highway is Gilgit, and you can take a PIA flight from Islamabad to Gilgit.
facts.quote: usual jumping off point is Gilgit

facts.text: The highway runs from Abbottabad to the border in Pakistan, and to Kashgar in China.
facts.quote: runs from Abbottabad to the border

facts.text: You can hire a jeep to enter the Chapursan Valley, where guesthouses exist in some villages.
Driving direction changes at the Chinese-Pakistani border.
facts.quote: Driving direction changes at the Chinese-Pakistani border.

facts.text: There is SCOM cell signal in Sost, but internet is very slow during peak hours.
facts.quote: SCOM cell signal in the town

facts.text: Check local reports before the trip and avoid adventuring if it rains or snows heavily; extra caution is required in winter.
facts.quote: Extra caution is required in the winter.

facts.text: Obey suggested speed limits, which change with the season or weather events.
facts.quote: change with the season or weather events

facts.text: Winds can be very strong and frigid, so carry a lot of warm clothing.
facts.quote: Winds can be very strong and frigid

facts.text: At the Sost immigration office, travelers must go through the entry and exit process and fill out a health declaration form. It can be busy and chaotic, so arrive with plenty of time.
facts.quote: fill out a health declaration form

facts.text: Mind altitude sickness: many people get symptoms already if sleeping at 2,500 m without acclimatization, and 3,500 m is regarded as very high in this context. Carry an oxygen mask if you have chronic respiratory conditions or feel unwell.
Tickets to Tashkurgan from NATCO cost 1500-2000, while Xinjiang Gawadar International costs 2500.
The Karakoram Highway lies in one of the safer parts of Pakistan, but expect inhospitable terrain. The more you go north, the safer it becomes, especially between Gilgit and the border pass.
facts.quote: The more you go north, the safer it becomes

facts.text: Many countries advise against all travel on the highway between Mansehra and Chilas via Battagram, Besham City, Dasu and Sazin up to the junction with the N15, due to poor road safety.
facts.quote: Many countries advise against all travel on the highway between Mansehra and Chilas

facts.text: Beware of avalanches and landslides. Before thinking of going on the trip, check local reports and avoid adventuring if it rains or snows heavily. Extra caution is required in the winter.
